claimed_purpose.text: TeleMem is positioned as a memory system for agents, addressing histories beyond context windows, multi-character isolation, video memory, and low-latency retrieval.
TeleMem is positioned as an agent-memory system evaluated against benchmark tasks requiring persistent memory across conversations.
TeleMem provides text memory (and optionally video memory) for agents, installable as a core package or with extras.
TeleMem is described as having a comprehensive and advanced memory management system with multimodal extensions
TeleMem can act as a drop-in replacement for mem0, providing memory storage and retrieval for agents or chains.
TeleMem is described as local-first, disabling mem0's anonymized PostHog telemetry by default.

mechanisms.text: Write path: add_memory accepts either a single text statement or a list of conversation turns (role/content messages). By default it runs an LLM inference step to extract salient facts before storing; setting infer=false stores raw text as-is.
TeleMem applies a similarity threshold when comparing memories, used to determine when two memories are considered the same (relevant to deduplication or conflict/supersession on write).
Per-run message log: a deep copy of the base message list is made at the start of each run, so conversation state is isolated to a single invocation and not persisted across calls
add_mm() ingests a raw video into persistent memory through three cached stages: frame extraction, caption generation, and vector database embedding of clip captions.
Write path (infer=True): latest turn is summarized against earlier turns, embedded, matched against similar memories, LLM-fused, and dual-written to FAISS + JSON.
TeleMem buffers events up to a configurable maximum before flushing them to a vector store, distinguishing a transient buffer from persisted vector storage.
Action-conditional evaluation (MEMTRACK-style) is planned for the MCP server, suggesting the MCP server component has a store/action-linked memory path.
Video database (vector store) is initialised once and reused across runs — this is the only state that persists across questions within a session
Event/conversation-level memories are kept under a separate pseudo-user scope 'events' and are searched automatically alongside user memories.
Tool results are appended to the in-turn message list as 'tool' role messages; they are not extracted into a separate curated memory store
On-policy evaluation is planned, where the agent's behavior shapes what gets stored — implying a write path driven by agent interaction.
Storage format: FAISS index for retrieval plus JSON metadata for human-readable auditability, organized by session and character
The integration pattern is explicitly described as retrieve-then-prompt: search() before answering, add() after each exchange.
Ingestion and query are distinct measured operations, implying a separate store (ingestion) and retrieve (query) path.
Retrieve policy: search always includes shared events memories regardless of which character profile is queried.
The store is per-video: one NanoVectorDB file per video, isolated by video name in a dedicated subdirectory.
Delete, update, history, and reset operations are inherited from mem0 and available on the TeleMem object.
Change history: a per-memory audit log of ADD/UPDATE/DELETE events is retrievable via memory.history().
Isolation is per user_id (character profile); each user_id gets an independent memory profile.
Write is skipped if the database file already exists; no update or merge logic is applied.
Memory is isolated per character, searchable by character identity
search() returns results in a mem0-compatible shape.
TeleMem includes a video memory capability.

def _get_buffer_key(self, run_id: str, user_id: Optional[str]) -> str:

    return f"{run_id}_{mem_type}"
